main_text.p: mufque (3.) interea exspirare spiritus validos & igneos, atque attrahere alium aërem, atque alium (4.) à præcedente attrahi; cum quo (5.) accedant illi spiritus vitrioli & sanguinis; qui (6.) inventes proprium originem, ibi sistantur, & cum spiritibus vitriolica (7.) vulneri se infinuent, & fanent. Idem fere Helmontio respondisse Gaffendum olim, subjungit D. Strauss, sed non tam clarè, non tam dilucidè, nec ita καθ' ἕκαστον ut prolata hæc sunt ab Illustr. Comite. Dicebat Helmontius, inquit, curationes tales fieri eo modo, quo apparet ignis advolare ad naphtham distantem: Siquidem, ut hæc involatio non fit, nisi quia exnaphtha funditur pinguis halitus, qui in sui extremo accensus, ad ipsam usque naphtham, ex qua prodit, continuatione inflammatur; ita Medicamenti Sympathetici vim involare in diffitum vulnus, quatenus concipiendum est, diffusum esse aliquid à vulnere usque ad remedium illud, quod in sui extremo, re-

page.notes: Marginal reference numerals (3)–(7) are printed in the text. Page number and signature read from the scan; the foot-of-page word "medio" is the catchword-like continuation. Greek phrase "καθ' ἕκαστον" is a conjectural reading of the printed Greek, marked for checking. Several words in the first lines are heavily damaged and may be misread.
